tests.description: Timed check on Social & Cultural Influences on Dance

questions.question: Q: How did social and political conditions influence Christopher Bruce's Ghost Dances?
questions.correctAnswer: Ghost Dances was inspired by the political oppression in Latin America. Bruce used traditional folk dance imagery and the motif of ghostly figures to represent the disappeared, reflecting the social injustice and violence of the period.

questions.question: Q: Explain one way technology has changed how dance is created or performed.
questions.correctAnswer: Projection and digital scenography allow choreographers to create immersive environments that interact with dancers, such as in Akram Khan's work where digital backdrops extend the narrative beyond the physical body.

questions.question: Q: How have gender roles in dance changed over time?
questions.correctAnswer: Historically, ballet portrayed women as delicate and ethereal while men displayed strength. Contemporary choreographers such as Matthew Bourne have challenged this — his male Swan Lake redefines gender representation, and many works now explore fluid and non-traditional gender roles.

questions.question: Q: Why is understanding social and cultural context important for AQA 8236?
questions.correctAnswer: The AQA specification requires students to analyse how context informs choreographic intention and meaning. Understanding the social and cultural influences behind prescribed works enables deeper, more informed analysis.

questions.question: Q: Give an example of how multiculturalism has influenced contemporary dance.
questions.correctAnswer: Akram Khan's work blends Kathak with contemporary dance, creating a fusion that draws on his Bangladeshi heritage and Western training. This cross-cultural approach produces a unique movement vocabulary that communicates themes of identity and belonging.
